metadata.summary: Brian McDermott has warned his England side not to chase the points as they look to keep their slim Rugby League World Cup hopes alive with a big win against Papua New Guinea.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England's Brian McDermott admits side face 'unique task' to progress and can't get distracted | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: England's Brian McDermott admits side face 'unique task' to progress and can't get distracted England head coach Brian McDermott speaks to the media on Thursday, as his side seek to avoid historic Rugby League World Cup pool stage exit; England face Papua New Guinea in their final pool fixture on Friday (9.05am kick-off), knowing they need a big win to keep semi-final hopes alive Thursday 29 October 2026 11:13, UK Image: England head coach Brian McDermott spoke to media on Thursday as his side seek to avoid a historic first World Cup pool-stage exit Brian McDermott has warned his England side not to chase the points as they look to keep their slim Rugby League World Cup hopes alive with a big win against Papua New Guinea. England are up against it in their bid to make it through to the semi-finals after they lost 30-12 to Tonga in their opening game. They must beat Papua New Guinea in their final pool game in Woollongong on Friday and then wait until Sunday, when they need Tonga to beat Samoa, upon whom England must also make up a 68-point deficit. That means tries will be the order of the day against Papua New Guinea but McDermott, who saw his side beat France 82-0 in their second game , has called for patience. messages.text: Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Pohankova at Pan Pacific Open in Japan

metadata.summary: Naomi Osaka, seeded No 7 and playing before home fans in Japan, was knocked out of the Pan Pacific Open on Thursday by teenager Mia Pohankova.
metadata.content: Pan Pacific Open: Naomi Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Mia Pohankova and knocked out in front of home crowd in Tokyo | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Pan Pacific Open: Naomi Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Mia Pohankova and knocked out in front of home crowd in Tokyo Japan's Naomi Osaka stunned in front of home crowd as she is knocked out by Slovakian teenager Mia Pohankova in Tokyo exit; You can watch the WTA Pan Pacific Open, WTA Guangzhou Open, ATP Swiss Indoors and ATP Vienna Open live on Sky Sports Tennis Thursday 29 October 2026 08:23, UK Image: Japan's former world No. 1 Naomi Osaka was stunned in Tokyo as she lost to Slovakian teenager Mia Pohankova Naomi Osaka, seeded No 7 and playing before home fans in Japan, was knocked out of the Pan Pacific Open on Thursday by teenager Mia Pohankova. Slovakia's Pohankova, who turned 18 a week ago and was a wild-card entry in Japan, upset Osaka 6-3 7-5 to advance to the quarter-finals. Pohankova will face Alycia Parks in the last eight. Pohankova, the 2025 junior singles champion at Wimbledon, stunned Osaka, who was coming off a win over Jasmine Paolini in the first round in Tokyo. messages.text: Toney trial date for alleged assault set for 2028

metadata.summary: England striker Ivan Toney will face trial over an alleged assault at a London nightclub in summer 2028.
metadata.content: Ivan Toney: Trial for England striker over alleged assault is set for June 2028 | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ivan Toney: Trial for England striker over alleged assault is set for June 2028 England striker Ivan Toney has pleaded not guilty to a charge of assault occasioning bodily harm; trial date has been set for June 2028; nightclub incident occurred in December 2025; Toney appeared in Southwark Crown Court on Thursday and formally entered not guilty plea Thursday 29 October 2026 11:43, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England striker Ivan Toney has pleaded not guilty in court after being accused of headbutting and punching a man at a nightclub in London last year. England striker Ivan Toney will face trial over an alleged assault at a London nightclub in summer 2028. The 30-year-old is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on December 6 last year. Toney appeared at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday morning and formally entered a not guilty plea to a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm. During the five-minute hearing, a provisional trial date was set for the same court on June 12, 2028 by Judge Christopher Hehir, who told the defendant he was "sorry" about the delay. messages.text: Sir Harry? Kane responds to knighthood talk after Ballon d'Or win

metadata.summary: Harry Kane would be "massively proud" to be knighted, but admits it would be "weird" to have everyone calling him Sir.
metadata.content: Harry Kane: Ballon d'Or 2026 winner responds to knighthood possibility after being crowned world's best | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Harry Kane: Ballon d'Or 2026 winner responds to knighthood possibility after being crowned world's best England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or for 25 years on Monday after a stellar season for club and country in which he scored 73 goals across all competitions, prompting talk of a knighthood for the 33-year-old Thursday 29 October 2026 11:04, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Prime Minister Andy Burnham congratulates England captain Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or. Harry Kane would be "massively proud" to be knighted, but admits it would be "weird" to have everyone calling him Sir. The England and Bayern Munich striker won the Ballon d'Or award on Monday night after a stellar year for club and country, and has been priced at 3-1 by some bookmakers to be knighted by 2030. Speaking about the prospect of a knighthood after Bayern's DFB-Pokal win over Magdeburg, Kane told reporters: "I wouldn't say no to it, that's for sure. "If it happens it'll be incredible, and something I'll be massively proud of. But I don't want to get too carried away."
